auto_merge.commit_title: [KV Offload] Expose the processed prefix at request finalization (#57646)

repo.description: A high-throughput and memory-efficient inference and serving engine for LLMs
repo.name: vllm

detail.body:
## Purpose

[#51787](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51787) (f12fe10c5c) removed repeated scheduler touch() calls and introduced key positions for request-scoped recency handling. Those positions can include the full prompt before execution completes, so they cannot distinguish the processed prefix from an untouched suffix when a request terminates early.

Expose num_computed_tokens, num_in_flight_tokens, num_prompt_tokens, and num_tokens as read-only ReqContext properties that delegate to Request and stay up to date. These allow offload backends to derive the processed-prefix boundary, excluding in-flight work and the uncommitted final sampled token. Contexts without an associated Request return None. The complete key-position map remains available for outstanding transfers.

Since ReqContext now retains a reference to Request, release completed-batch context references in the async lookup worker before it waits for another batch.

This is separate from [#54979](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54979) and [#43569](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43569), which address GPU cache registration and rollback, and [#52103](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52103), which carries provenance through stored events. This PR exposes metadata; it does not change existing eviction policies.

## Test Plan

- Added a scheduler context test checking that token counts reflect subsequent request updates and return None for contexts without a request.
- Added an async lookup regression test checking that completed request contexts are released while the worker remains idle.

## Test Result

All 20 isolated checks passed using the relevant production definitions and repository tests.

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("registered", [True, False])
+def test_req_context_counts_live_until_request_finished(registered):
+    """Finished counts survive late outputs and request cleanup."""
+
+    class RequestStub(SimpleNamespace):
+        pass
+
+    counts = dict(
+        num_computed_tokens=0,
+        num_in_flight_tokens=16,
+        num_prompt_tokens=64,
+        num_tokens=80,
+    )
+    request = RequestStub(
+        request_id="req", kv_transfer_params=None, kv_hints=None, **counts
+    )
+    request_ref = weakref.ref(request)
+    scheduler = object.__new__(OffloadingConnectorScheduler)
+    scheduler.config = SimpleNamespace(kv_group_configs=())
+    scheduler.manager = MagicMock(spec=OffloadingManager)
+    scheduler._step_region = None
+    scheduler._req_status = {}
+
+    def on_new_request(ctx):
+        assert {name: getattr(ctx, name) for name in counts} == counts
+        return RequestOffloadingContext()
+
+    scheduler.manager.on_new_request.side_effect = on_new_request
+    if registered:
+        scheduler.on_new_request(request)
+        ctx = scheduler.manager.on_new_request.call_args.args[0]
+        for name in counts:
+            counts[name] += 16
+            setattr(request, name, counts[name])
+        assert {name: getattr(ctx, name) for name in counts} == counts
+
+    scheduler.request_finished(request)
+    ctx = scheduler.manager.on_new_request.call_args.args[0]
+    for name in counts:
+        setattr(request, name, 0)
+    assert {name: getattr(ctx, name) for name in counts} == counts
+    scheduler._req_status.clear()
+    del request
+    assert request_ref() is None
+    assert {name: getattr(ctx, name) for name in counts} == counts
+
+    synthetic = ReqContext(req_id="synthetic")
+    assert all(getattr(synthetic, name) is None for name in counts)
+
+

This field seems non-intuitive to me (unlike num_computed_tokens or num_prompt_tokens for example).
Can we consider exposing other fields instead (which can be used to derived this specific num_processed_tokens)?
Also, this is set only at request_finished.
I suggest we expose `@property`-ies which delegate to `Request`, and are always up-to-date.

inline_comments.body:
One lifecycle concern: secondary-tier `on_request_finished` can run after the connector removes the request from `_req_status`, for example with deferred cascades or during cache reset. PR #60469 needs the counters at that point.

The direct reference preserves the live-property behavior we introduced following your earlier feedback. Keeping it with the single `del` seems simpler than introducing snapshots or extending scheduler bookkeeping, although it retains the Request longer. Is scheduler-only ownership worth that additional complexity here?
